questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In [Amines & Biomolecules], aniline is subjected to diazotization with $\text{NaNO}_2 + \text{HCl}$ at $0-5^\circ\text{C}$ to form $[A]$. Reaction of $[A]$ with $\text{CuCN}$ yields $[B]$, which upon complete acidic hydrolysis gives $[C]$. Reduction of $[C]$ with $\text{LiAlH}_4$ yields what final product $[D]$?
questions.solution: Diazotization gives benzenediazonium chloride $[A]$. Sandmeyer cyanidation gives benzonitrile $[B]$. Acidic hydrolysis of the cyano group gives benzoic acid $[C]$. Strong reduction of benzoic acid by $\text{LiAlH}_4$ yields benzyl alcohol $[D]$.
questions.explanation: Deduce using established organic reaction mechanisms in Amines & Biomolecules.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In [Amines & Biomolecules], an aliphatic primary amide on treatment with bromine and aqueous $\text{KOH}$ (Hoffmann degradation) yields an amine containing $3$ carbon atoms. How many carbon atoms were present in the precursor amide?
questions.solution: Hoffmann bromamide degradation eliminates the carbonyl carbon as carbonate: $\text{R-CONH}_2 \to \text{R-NH}_2$. If the product amine has 3 carbon atoms, the starting amide had $3 + 1 = 4$ carbon atoms (butanamide).
questions.explanation: Solve using reaction stoichiometry in Amines & Biomolecules.
